packets.title: glia-stamp: one PARSER_STAMP per commit however the tree is checked out or packaged - `src` tested on the workspace-relative key, Cargo.lock hashed over the HASHED_ROOTS crates' dependency closure only (ruling STAMP-LOCK)
packets.area: F0 - build stamp reproducibility (follow-up from FE.5, W1)
packets.rationale: FE.5 (W1) blocked on its step (h): an sdist build of glia-cli printed a different BUILD_STAMP from the wheel of the same commit. Two causes (FE.5's probes, /home/ivy/.cache/glia-FE.5/): (1) stamp/build.rs is_input tests for a `src` component on the ABSOLUTE path, so a tree under any directory named `src` (uv builds sdists in ~/.cache/uv/sdists-v9/.../src) hashes tests/, examples/ and benches/ too: 537 inputs instead of 304; (2) the stamp hashes the whole Cargo.lock, and `maturin sdist` trims workspace members to glia-cli's path deps, so cargo prunes glia-py / glia-toy-domain / pyo3* / inventory / target-lexicon from the lock and the stamp moves. James 2026-10-24 ruled STAMP-LOCK ('Hash only what glia uses'): same commit = same stamp however it is built. A calibration record is read only by the BUILD_STAMP that wrote it (EC.1), so a drifting stamp silently discards calibration.
entry_points: stamp/build.rs - is_input / rel_key / main's HASHED_FILES handling
packets.implementation:
0. Read stamp/build.rs at HEAD (HASHED_ROOTS, HASHED_FILES, rel_key, is_input, visit, main) and FE.5's probes (/home/ivy/.cache/glia-FE.5/fnv.py, fnv_abs.py, inputs.py, run1.log). Write the tests first and record their failing baseline.
1. is_input takes the workspace-relative key (rel_key's output) and tests for a `src` component there, never on the absolute path. Behaviour inside the workspace is unchanged: the input set at HEAD stays the same 304 files (pin the count as HEAD's, measured).
2. Cargo.lock: instead of hashing the file's bytes, parse its [[package]] tables by hand (no new crate: F0.2 is the release's one lock move; a build-script dependency would move the lock) - name, version, source, checksum, dependencies. Seed the closure with the package names of the HASHED_ROOTS crates (read each root's Cargo.toml [package] name; a root without one is skipped), walk `dependencies` entries (`name`, `name version`, `name version (source)`: resolve by name, and by name + version when several versions are locked), and hash one line per closure package, `name version source checksum`, sorted. A grammar bump (tree-sitter-* version or checksum) moves the stamp; removing packages outside the closure (glia-py, glia-toy-domain, pyo3*, inventory, target-lexicon, glia-cli's own bin deps) does not. A lock the parser cannot read is a build failure via die(), never a silent fallback.
3. stamp/tests/stamp_inputs.rs (or unit tests in the build script's testable helpers if the crate's layout needs it - say which): (a) the same tree copied under a directory named `src` gives the same input list and stamp; (b) a Cargo.lock with the py / toy-domain members and their exclusive deps removed gives the same lock digest; (c) a tree-sitter grammar version or checksum change moves it; (d) a closure package's dependency added moves it.
4. Declare the one-off PARSER_STAMP move (the lock digest's input changes form) in the commit body: every parse cache and calibration record is rebuilt once.

packets.title: GPU embeddings by default: the ORT WebGPU execution provider (Dawn over Vulkan / Metal / D3D12) in a crash-isolated worker process, CPU fallback on any failure, CUDA as an opt-in build feature, the device on every vector row
packets.rationale: James 2026-10-25 ("it shouldn't be an optional tbf a default ... even a 1660 super can do it"; "Everything you mentioned seems reasonable for web gpu including child processes"). bge-small at the 512-token cut is compute-bound on CPU (~8.5 texts/s on a Ryzen 3700X, batch size irrelevant 8..256), so a first `glia embed` of a glia-sized repo (~33k nodes) costs ~25 min per recipe. The 2026-10-25 spike (~/.cache/glia-gpu-spike (fe-bench/src/main.rs, ort-raw/src/main.rs, scripts/compare.py)) on a GTX 1660 Super, CPU shared with the FB.6 gate (lower bounds): CPU 5.4-6.3/s; ORT WebGPU EP (ort 2.0.0-rc.13, Dawn -> Vulkan) 30.4/s at batch 8, 0.57 GiB VRAM, throughput halves above 8 and the PROCESS ABORTS (free(): invalid pointer, core dump) at batch >= 64; ORT CUDA EP (fastembed 4.9.1 + ort/cuda, pip CUDA 12 / cuDNN 9 libs, 2.7 GB) 59.9-66.1/s at batch 8-64, OOM (clean Err) at 128/256 on 6 GB. Every route: max abs diff vs CPU fastembed < 4e-7, min cosine 0.99999988, top-10 overlap 10/10 on 10 queries.

embed/src/fast.rs - FastEmbedder::new takes a Device: `with_execution_providers([..].error_on_failure())`, sub-batches of `batch(device)` fed one at a time (fastembed's own batch split never runs two batches concurrently on the GPU)
cli: a hidden `glia embed-worker` subcommand calling glia_embed::worker_main (the CLI's worker binary is itself); py: the worker the wheel runs (see implementation 4)
packets.implementation:
Built on the spike's scratch code (read it first: ~/.cache/glia-gpu-spike (fe-bench/src/main.rs, ort-raw/src/main.rs, scripts/compare.py); it reimplements fastembed's pipeline over raw ort rc.13 and has the CPU / WebGPU / CUDA harness and the compare script).
1. Bump fastembed to =6.0.0 / ort =2.0.0-rc.13; adapt FastEmbedder to the 6.0 API. Run the dependency + licence check; record the crate count delta in the commit body. The CPU vectors move ~3e-7 (ORT 1.20 -> 1.28): declared.
2. device.rs as in entry_points. Selection order: GLIA_EMBED_DEVICE=cpu -> Cpu, fallback=override; =webgpu / =cuda -> that device, failure is a hard error naming it; unset -> WebGpu if built, else Cpu fallback=not_built; a WebGpu session that fails to commit (no adapter, no Vulkan ICD: the spike saw a clean Err from WebGpuContext::Initialize RequestAdapterStatus under error_on_failure) -> Cpu, fallback=no_adapter:<first line of the error>. Without error_on_failure ORT silently runs on CPU: never omit it. Cuda is only ever explicit (GLIA_EMBED_DEVICE=cuda) and only in a gpu-cuda build; a CUDA OOM (clean Err) halves the batch once, then falls back to Cpu, fallback=oom.
3. worker.rs: the GPU session always runs in the child. The parent embeds through it; if the child exits abnormally (signal, abort, non-zero, broken pipe) the parent re-embeds the remaining texts on a CPU FastEmbedder in-process and reports fallback=gpu_crash:<signal or status>. A clean error frame is fallback=<reason>. The CPU path never spawns a child. One child per process (FB.4's one-FastEmbedder rule), started lazily, reused across calls, killed on drop.
4. Surfaces: the CLI's worker is `glia embed-worker` (hidden from cli/surface: assert it is absent from `glia --help` and the surface files). glia-py: ship the worker in the wheel (a small binary target of glia-embed, `glia-embed-worker`, installed through maturin's data/scripts or bundled next to the extension and found by path relative to the module); if the worker binary is absent or unrunnable, CPU in-process with fallback=no_worker. Pick the mechanism that the wheel smoke tests can verify on Linux; record which in docs/embeddings.md.
5. Packaging: the WebGPU build links ORT statically and NEEDS libwebgpu_dawn.so (~12 MB). A missing Dawn library stops the binary from starting at all, so it must be bundled with an $ORIGIN rpath (Linux: auditwheel or copy + patchelf; Windows: the DLL beside the exe / extension; macOS: @loader_path) in both wheels' workflows, and scripts/check-cli-wheel.sh must run the installed wheel in a clean venv with no Vulkan ICD (VK_DRIVER_FILES=/nonexistent.json) and see fallback=no_adapter, never a load failure. CUDA stays out of every published wheel (650 MB provider + user CUDA 12 / cuDNN 9).
6. Rows: code-domain VectorRow gains an optional `device` field (cpu | webgpu | cuda; absent = cpu, so old rows read as before); embed_repo writes it. FB.4's index treats rows of another device as fresh (the vectors agree to 4e-7); a row's device never decides staleness.
7. Marker beside the existing `[embed] model load` line, once per embedder: `[embed] device=<adapter name> backend=<cpu|webgpu|cuda> driver=<v> fallback=<reason|none> batch=<n>`. Dawn's `maxDynamic... artificially reduced` warning is filtered from the worker's stderr.
8. Tests and gates stay CPU-pinned: every test that embeds with bge-small, and the FB.6 embedding gate harness, set GLIA_EMBED_DEVICE=cpu, so CI on hosted runners is unchanged. An `#[ignore]`d GPU test (run by hand on James's 1660 Super) embeds the spike's 256 texts on WebGPU and asserts max abs diff < 1e-5 vs CPU and top-10 overlap 10/10.
9. docs/embeddings.md: devices, the override, the fallback reasons, the batch pins and why (the abort at >= 64), the per-platform support table, the issue template's ask (the marker line, OS, whether GLIA_EMBED_DEVICE=cpu works).
10. Clean numbers: once no other CPU job runs, rerun the spike harness (CPU at batch 256, WebGPU at batch 8, CUDA at 32 if the pip libs are still in the spike venv) and put the table in the commit body and docs/embeddings.md.

1. FIX THE CONFIGURATION FROM FB.6's (seen) data, before any held-out run, and commit it in the rule: recipe t2, query form bge prefix (SEMp:t2, the best fused form in FB.6's information rows), fusion FUSE[X,Y] = 0.5 minmax(X) + 0.5 minmax(Y) exactly as FB.6 defines it, no weight tuning. Candidates: F1 = FUSE[T1s,SEMp:t2]; F2 = LX[IDR, FUSE[T1s,SEMp:t2]] (the shipped find --files order with its BM25 part replaced by the blend: ids still route first). 2. THE PASS RULE (strictness as FB-5, James 2026-10-24 "Strict"): panel = the six public snapshots of bench/rank-gate/snapshots.json; metric recall@10 in rank_eval's find shape; every a - b is --gate-pair's paired commit-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (B = 1000) on the panel's test commits only. R1: F1 - T1s has CI lo > 0 on >= 5 of 6 and hi >= 0 on all 6. R2: F2 - LX[IDR,T1s] has CI lo > 0 on >= 3 of 6 and hi >= 0 on all 6. PASS = R1 and R2. packets.title: Language-group resolution speed: the TS superclass pass stops walking every unresolved call (measured 8.1 s for 207 edges on twenty), and resolve_calls / resolve_refs run per call site on the engine pool and join in input order, so a large single-language group no longer builds on one core
packets.rationale: James 2026-10-30: 'Wouldn't be better to use the threads to quick pool and sort everything then quick join ?' and 'we have a general fix to packet'. Measured 2026-10-30 (release, cold, per-second core samples + timestamped stderr markers): twenty (34.6k TS files, cohort pin 8fd53a83) builds in 31 s, of which 0-6 s run on 11-16 cores (walk / parse) and ~24 s on exactly one core. Inside build_ts_like (graph/src/build.rs): merge + symbol table + imports 1.4 s, resolve_calls 8.3 s (9.3 -> 17.6 s, between the `[imports] reexport` and `[recv] constructed receivers` markers), refs / member reads 1.3 s, resolve_inherited_calls + emit_override_implements 8.1 s (19.0 -> 27.1 s, ending at `[ts-inherit] calls bound through superclasses: 207 ..`), then passes 1.2 s and persist 2 s. The engine pool (engine/src/parallel.rs) already sizes itself to every core, but it parallelises ACROSS language groups: one group is one serial graph build, so any repo dominated by one language (TS monorepos first; a large Go, JVM, Python or C++ tree would hit the same path) builds mostly on one core. glia itself (26 groups, 3.5 s) is unaffected. Two different problems: the superclass pass is per-site waste (it re-walks every still-unresolved call, most of which no superclass can bind), the call / ref passes are real work over read-only indexes.
entry_points: graph/src/calls.rs: resolve_inherited_calls (~line 2068: loops over every g.unresolved_calls site, self_lookup / receiver_lookup / nearest_definer per site), emit_override_implements, superclasses, receiver_class

graph/src/calls.rs: resolve_calls (~line 183: one loop over `calls`, reads g, pushes edges and g.unresolved_calls, keeps stat counters and the BareFieldGate / ConstructedReceivers / StateReads / ClassScopeReceivers / TsReceivers tallies) and resolve_refs (~line 656)

graph/src/build.rs: build_ts_like and every other builder calling resolve_calls / resolve_refs (build_python, build_go_passes, build_rust, build_dart, build_swift, build_elixir, build_c_cpp, build_ruby, build_dotted)
engine/src/parallel.rs: par_map_ordered (read only; already nests on a rayon worker, which the language build runs on); engine/src/build/lang_build.rs: the builder calls
packets.implementation:
PART A - the superclass pass (do this first; it is the cheaper half and must not be hidden by threads).
1. Measure before changing anything: profile `target/release/glia build <twenty copy>` (`cargo install samply` then `samply record --save-only`, user-space sampling of your own process works at perf_event_paranoid 2; if it does not, time the pass's helpers with temporary Instant timers you do not commit). Record which of superclasses / enclosing_class_or_struct / receiver_class / BareFieldGate::admits / nearest_definer / push_edge holds the 8.1 s, and how many sites the loop visits. Quote the numbers in the commit body.
2. Fix the measured cost. The expected shape is an EXACT prefilter: nearest_definer can only succeed for a member name that some ancestor class (a class that is in some `supers` list) declares, so build that name set once and keep a site out of every lookup when its name is not in it (it stays in `kept`, in its original order). If the profile shows a different cost (a linear scan inside a helper, a per-site rebuild of an index), fix that instead. The pass's output must not change: same edges, same order, same kept list, same `[ts-inherit]` counts. Same for emit_override_implements if the profile shows it.
PART B - pooled resolution, for every builder.
3. The graph crate gains no dependency (Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock never move in a packet: constraint `lock`). Define in graph/src/calls.rs a small pub trait the engine implements, e.g. `pub trait ResolvePool: Sync { fn map_chunks(&self, n: usize, f: &(dyn Fn(std::ops::Range<usize>) -> ChunkOut + Sync)) -> Vec<ChunkOut>; }` with whatever concrete output type the passes need, plus a sequential impl the graph crate's own callers and tests use. engine/src/build/lang_build.rs implements it over crate::parallel::par_map_ordered (it already nests on the worker the language build runs on); do not edit engine/src/parallel.rs (FH.22 owns it this wave). Keep every existing pub builder signature: add a pooled entry the engine calls (e.g. a `_pooled` variant or a pool argument on the pub(crate) passes) so glia_graph's flat API stays additive; if you must change a pub signature, declare api_signature.
4. Split resolve_calls into decide (read-only &RepoGraph, per call site: the bound target + branch / evidence, or unresolved, plus that site's stat increments) and apply (in input order: push edges, push unresolved sites, sum the tallies). Chunks of contiguous sites run on the pool; apply walks the chunk outputs in chunk order, so the edge list, g.unresolved_calls and every marker count are byte-for-byte what the serial loop produced. The per-site mutable helpers (BareFieldGate, ConstructedReceivers, ..) become per-chunk and merge, IF they only count; if one caches a decision that later sites read, prove the cache is pure (same answer either way) or keep it serial and say so. extra_hook must be Sync to run pooled: a builder whose hook is not Sync (check GoPackages, rust_paths, CppScope, SwiftModuleTypes, ElixirModules, dart::provider_call) stays serial, listed in the marker. Same split for resolve_refs.
5. Marker, once per group build that ran pooled: `[resolve-pool] lang=<ext family> calls=<n> refs=<m> chunks=<c> threads=<t> calls_ms=<a> refs_ms=<b> serial_hooks=<list|->`; and `[ts-inherit] .. prefiltered=<k>` gains the count Part A kept out.
6. engine/tests/resolve_pool.rs: a multi-file TS fixture with classes, receivers, re-exports and inherited calls, plus a Go and a Rust fixture: the merged graph's nodes / edges / unresolved lists are identical under the sequential impl and the pooled one (call the graph passes both ways), and a GLIA_THREADS=1 vs default `generate_one` gives byte-identical persisted layouts (the byte_identical test's helper shape).

Quote the before / after `[timing] repo=.. language_build=` values and the total wall (before: language_build ~19.3 s, wall ~31 s); the superclass pass and resolve_calls each drop measurably, stated as measured numbers. (3) glia itself (a scratch `git clone --shared` of this repo): same byte-identity check, wall not worse. (4) The rank gate fast tier stays 0 drops (graph content is unchanged, so this is a sanity check).

packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge-precision audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, Under floor, ACCESSES_DATA|fact p 0.467, cluster A1, 5 of 8 wrong): extractor:data_sources matched `android.database.sqlite` inside JNI type-descriptor strings of jnigen-generated bindings (flutter/samples experimental/pedometer lib/health_connect.dart and src/health_connect/health_connect.c, data_source:sqlite and data_source:database_sql, 4 rows) and `Redis` inside `Redistribution` in a licence string (varfont_shader_puzzle wallpapers_flow.dart, 1 row). The probe at HEAD reproduces all five shapes and shows why: data_sources.rs's PATTERNS are substrings, and FD.5a / FD.5b made `guard.admits_name` admit every Dart / C string literal (a library is named in an import string), so a descriptor string and a licence string are read like `import 'package:redis/redis.dart'`. `database/sql` is no separate hit: it is the prefix of `android/database/sqlite`. The same substring rule also mints data_source:prisma from a UI string `'Prismatic colours'` (probe), so the word rule is not limited to Redis. The fix is two shape rules on an occurrence, keyed on the text around it, not on the file: a blanket skip of generated files (generated.rs's banner classifier, which the dev note names) would also drop sqlc's / Prisma's generated clients, which really do open a database.

Redistribution. You may reproduce';` mints nothing, `'Prismatic colours'` mints nothing, `'Resending'` mints nothing; (d) controls: `import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';` -> sqlite, `final c = RedisConnection();` -> redis, Go `import "database/sql"` -> database_sql, Go `import "modernc.org/sqlite"` -> sqlite (a slash path that is no descriptor), Java `import org.redisson.Redisson;` -> redis, TS `new IORedis()` / `Redis.createClient()` / C# `using StackExchange.Redis;` -> redis, `@prisma/client` + `new PrismaClient()` -> prisma. The existing FD.6 Rust tests stay green unchanged. 2. `in_jvm_descriptor(source, at)`: from `at`, walk back over bytes in `[A-Za-z0-9_$/]` to the token start `s`; the byte before `s` must be one of `( ) ; [ " '` (or `s` is 0); strip a leading run of JVM primitive / array letters `[BCDFIJSZ]` from the token; the rest must start with `L`, hold a `/` before `at`, and the forward run from `at` over the same byte class must stop at `;` (the descriptor's end) or at a `/` immediately followed by a closing quote (jnigen's C splits a descriptor across adjacent literals). So `"modernc.org/sqlite"` (the run stops at `.`), `"Lib/sqlite/x.db"` (stops at `.`) and a Go `"database/sql"` import (no `L` start) are no descriptor. Language-blind: a JVM descriptor is the same text in Dart, C, C++, Kotlin and Java. 3. `word_tail_ok(source, at, pattern)`: for a pattern whose first byte is ASCII uppercase and whose last byte is an ASCII letter (Prisma, TypeORM, Sequelize, ActiveRecord, Redis, Memcached, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Algolia, Meilisearch, Typesense, SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, MongoClient, S3Client, BlobServiceClient), the byte after the occurrence must not be an ASCII lowercase letter (a camel tail `RedisTemplate`, a `.` / `(` / `;` / `:` / quote / space all pass); every other pattern (lowercase, dotted, `::`, path-shaped) is unchanged, so `memcache` still reads `memcached` and `psycopg` reads `psycopg2`. Add the row `("Redisson", DataSourceKind::Cache, "redis")` before `Redis` (Redisson's `Redis` is followed by `s`, which the tail rule refuses). 4. FD.4b's rule (`CodeGuard::opens_argument`) admits any statement literal that opens as a call argument, and these are call arguments: the callee is never asked. The probe at HEAD shows the shape is general: `std::fs::write(.., "INSERT INTO ledgers ..")`, Python `Path(..).write_text("CREATE TABLE ..")` and JS `fs.writeFileSync(.., "CREATE TABLE ..")` all mint entities (in JS opens_argument returns true before any callee check). FROM test_rows")` inside a `#[test]` fn of tests/seed_db.rs is refused (`[code-guard] data-entities lang=rust dropped=1`), while the same call in a helper fn of the same file mints `helper_rows`; parallel_build.rs's `write(..)` call sits in exactly such a helper. packets.title: yaml env: an `environment:` block whose file format defines it as something other than env vars - a pubspec.yaml's SDK constraints, a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI job's deployment environment - mints no `config:env:<key>`; docker-compose, serverless and every other `environment:` block keep their reading
packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, Under floor, cluster C1): DEFINES_CONFIG|fact judged p 0.667, 10 of 30 wrong, all 10 the same mechanism: extractor:yaml reads a flutter/samples pubspec.yaml `environment:` block (`sdk: ^3.x`, `flutter: ">=3.x"`, the Dart / Flutter SDK version constraints) as env vars `config:env:sdk` / `config:env:flutter` (bench/edge-audit/verdicts/mechanism.jsonl, e.g. `simplistic_editor::pubspec.yaml -> config:env:sdk`, `web::material_3_demo::pubspec.yaml -> config:env:flutter`). The cause is parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs `scan_compose_environment`: it reads every line that is exactly `environment:` in ANY .yml / .yaml file (engine/src/route.rs's yaml branch calls `extract_yaml_env_defs(source, module_id, repo)` with no path), so the block's children become env keys. The probe at HEAD reproduces the audit rows and finds the same mechanism in two more formats the audit did not sample: a GitHub Actions job's `environment: {name, url}` (a deployment environment) mints `config:env:name` / `config:env:url`, and a GitLab CI job's `environment: {name, url, on_stop}` mints `config:env:name` / `url` / `on_stop`. A structural rule (only an `environment:` under `services.<svc>`) would also drop correct readings: the probe's serverless `provider.environment.TABLE_NAME` is a real env var and is minted today, as are Ansible / Drone `environment:` maps. So the gate is by file format, where the format's own spec says `environment:` is not env vars: Dart pub (`pubspec.yaml`), GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/*.yml|yaml`), GitLab CI (`.gitlab-ci.yml`). The dev note scoped pubspec only; the two CI formats are added because the probe shows the same scanner misreading them (seed rule: do not fit the fix to the motivating case).

packets.title: walk: an in-repo directory symlink is not descended - its target is walked once, where it lies - and an out-of-repo directory symlink is walked once per canonical target with symlink cycles cut, so a mirrored tree (flutter/samples `web/<x> -> ../<x>`) or a link loop no longer indexes the same files under several qname prefixes
packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, Under floor, D3): the walk follows directory symlinks; flutter/samples has nine, `web/<x> -> ../<x>`, so each mirrored sample is indexed twice, under `web::<x>::..` and `<x>::..`, which made the `BasicTextField` doclink tie ambiguous (verdicts/mechanism.jsonl: `docs::web::simplistic_editor::README::replacements-layer -> simplistic_editor::lib::basic_text_field::BasicTextField`, judged wrong) and inflates every samples stratum's N. Measured on the rank-gate copy of that snapshot (~/.cache/glia-rank-gate/samples@291ba126bfc1, read-only `find`): 9 directory links, 159 .dart files reachable only through them. The mechanism is engine/src/walk.rs `walk_dir`: `path.is_dir()` follows symlinks and recurses with no visited set; nothing in walk.rs mentions symlinks (the only hit is FileStamp's 'Follows symlinks' doc). The probe at HEAD reproduces it (web/app -> ../app doubles every node) and finds two worse shapes: an in-repo cycle (`src/sub/up -> ..`) reads one file 41 times, and an out-of-repo cycle reached through two links reads one file 81 times (until the OS's ELOOP), with qnames 40 segments deep. What 'once' means: skip the LINK, walk the TARGET at its real path. The target is a real directory the walk reaches on its own, while the link is one alias of possibly several; the target's path is what git stores the content under (the link is a mode-120000 blob), what an editor opens and what CODE spans re-read; skipping the target would make qnames depend on name order and on a link's existence, and for a cycle the target is an ancestor that cannot be skipped. A directory link whose target is OUTSIDE the root is the only way its content enters the build, so it is still walked, once per canonical target (the first link in name order), and never into a directory already entered (cycle). File symlinks are deliberately unchanged: the only file link in the five audit / gate snapshots is shell's `src/floating_exceptions/src/config.ts -> ../../config.ts`, which sibling code imports (`import * as config from 'config'`) at the link's path, so skipping it would unbind a real import; they are counted, not skipped.

packets.title: doclink precision: a bare mention binds only an identifier-shaped token (a call `x()`, a `_` identifier, a mixed-case name), never a lone word, a registry name or a placeholder; a test / fixture / bench candidate binds only from a doc under its tree; an ambiguous tie prefers the doc's own project root before the least qname
packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, `## Under floor`, DOCUMENTS|derived p 0.387, 19 of 31 judged wrong) found two `pass:doclink` mechanisms. D1 (18): a backticked lone dictionary or command word (`graph` x2, `json`, `error`, `method`, `route`, `find`, `run`, `embed`, `location`, `impact`, `update`, `finding`), the edge-category name `CALLS` (x2) or the placeholder `PROJECT_ID` (microservices-demo docs/development-guide.md:63, 'Where `PROJECT_ID` is replaced by your Google Cloud project ID') binds a same-named symbol, mostly a test helper (activation::src::ppr_index::tests::graph), a test-local const (algo::classes::tests::CALLS), a substrate-gap fixture or bench code (bench::cohort::cohort::Glia::json); `model_shop` (a test dir) binds the CLI test method Scratch::model_shop. D2 (1): an ambiguous tie across sibling copies binds the least qname: flutter_maps_firestore's README `location` binds desktop_photo_search's generated PhotoBuilder.location, and web/simplistic_editor's `BasicTextField` binds the top-level copy. The probe reproduces every shape at HEAD c4152966 and measures the rule on glia's own tree: of 830 doclink edges, 549 bind a mention the shape / registry rule refuses and 42 more bind a test / bench candidate from a doc outside its tree (591 removed or re-bound; 239 kept, the 32 qualified ones included). A sampled 40 of the 549 holds about 6 correct binds (`hotspots` -> engine::hotspots, `splits`, `gaps`, `noop`), so the rule trades a little recall for most of the noise; the 12 SCREAMING_SNAKE constants glia's docs name (CODE_PASSES, INVOKED_MEMBERS, FORMAT_VERSION, WIDE_DAMPING ..) keep binding. packets.title: gRPC server registrations bind HANDLED_BY to the implementation they name (`addService(svc, { rpc: handler })`, `add_XServicer_to_server(impl, server)`, `RegisterXServer(s, impl)`), method by method, never to the enclosing function; an implementation built by another package's call (`health.NewServer()`) mints no in-repo handler
packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, HANDLED_BY|fact p 0.833, 5 of 30 wrong, all microservices-demo, `extractor:rpc_needles` rule `anchor`). H1 (4): the registration's enclosing function is bound: Node `loadAllProtos` (PaymentService and Health, src/paymentservice/server.js:88/95), Python `start()` (EmailService, email_server.py:52), Go `run()` (ProductCatalogService, server.go). H2 (1): shippingservice registers grpc's `health.NewServer()` for Health, yet the app's `server.Check` is bound. The mechanism is not in engine/src/build/rpc_needles.rs (it grafts and stamps rule `anchor`) but in parsers/code/extractors/src/grpc.rs `extract_grpc_server_nodes`: a `ServerShape::Register` hit names no type (`impl_for: None`), so (a) with no implementing type, ANY METHOD / FUNCTION of the file whose name folds to an rpc serves the service (H2: Health's Check), and (b) with no rpc method found, the registration line is anchored and `anchor::attach` makes its enclosing function the owner (H1). The probe reproduces all six wrong edges at HEAD c4152966 with the audit's exact qnames, and the three right handlers (ChargeServiceHandler, CheckHandler, DummyEmailService.SendOrderConfirmation) are absent.

parsers/code/extractors/src/anchor.rs `attach` / `owner_of_line` / `position_cell` (a marker's POSITION is its first anchor's line; every anchor line's enclosing METHOD / FUNCTION becomes a HANDLED_BY owner)
engine/src/build/rpc_needles.rs `apply_rpc_needles` (the per-file halves, then the sequential graft loop over `parses_by_lang`) and `graft_rpc_markers` (stamps `extractor:rpc_needles` rule `anchor`)

packets.implementation: 1. Read the implementation argument (grpc.rs): `ServerHit` gains `impl_arg: Option<ImplArg>`, filled for every Register shape from the call's argument text (balanced parens, the guard's code-only rule): Go `Register<S>Server(<srv>, <impl>)` arg 2; Python `add_<S>Servicer_to_server(<impl>, <server>)` arg 1; Node `addService(<def>, <impl>)` arg 2 (`node_add_service_hits` already parses arg 1); tonic `<S>Server::new(<impl>)` and ScalaPB `bindService(<impl>, ..)` arg 1. `ImplArg` is one of: `Type(name)` - `&T{..}` / `T{..}` / `T()` / `new T(..)` / `T::new(..)` / `T::default()`, or an identifier whose assignments in the enclosing function before the call (`x := &T{}`, `x = T()`, `var x = new T()`; several assignments -> each type, `None` skipped) all build in-file-resolvable types; `Handlers(Vec<(rpc, name)>)` - a Node object literal `{ rpc: <expr>, .. }` whose value is `Name`, `X.Name`, `this.Name` or `X.Name.bind(..)` (shorthand `{ sayHello }` too); `Foreign` - a call into another package (`pkg.F(..)` where `pkg` is an import alias / module name of the file: `health.NewServer()`, `health_pb2_grpc.HealthServicer()`), or an identifier bound only to one; `Unread` - anything else (a field, a parameter, a returned value). 2. Bind (`extract_grpc_server_nodes`): for a service with a Register hit, `Type(T)` -> the rpc methods of the in-file CLASS / STRUCT named T, else of the in-file classes T's header names as bases, up to 4 levels (Python `DummyEmailService(BaseEmailService)` serves Health through BaseEmailService.Check); `Handlers` -> for each (rpc, name) whose rpc folds to one of the service's (`fold_rpc_name`), the in-file METHOD / FUNCTION `name` (ChargeServiceHandler, CheckHandler); an inline function value binds nothing (counted). `Foreign` -> nothing. `Unread` -> today's fallback (any in-file METHOD / FUNCTION whose name folds to an rpc), and nothing else. A Register line is NEVER an owner anchor: `GrpcNodes` gains `sites: Vec<Anchor>` (marker POSITION lines that take no owner edge); `graft_rpc_markers` writes a marker's POSITION from its first anchor else its first site, and a marker with no anchor is CONTAINED by the file MODULE (`anchor::attach`'s to_module arm), never HANDLED_BY its enclosing function. Base-shape hits are unchanged. 3. Cross-file Go type (`Type(T)` with no T in the file): `GrpcNodes` gains `deferred: Vec<(NodeId, String, Vec<String>)>` (marker, type name, folded rpc names); after the graft loop `apply_rpc_needles` binds each against the Go parses of the same package directory: the STRUCT named T and its METHODs (nav parent) whose names fold to the rpcs, pushing marker -HANDLED_BY-> method onto the marker file's parse with EVIDENCE `extractor:rpc_needles` rule `register_impl`, skipping a pair the type's own file already anchors (its Base hit). Other languages: a type in another file stays unbound (counted `elsewhere`). This pass is not memoised (it reads other files), so a watch update re-derives it like a clean build. 4. Marker: grafts.rs's `[grpc-server-impl] <n> server markers from <k> known services repo=<label>` gains ` register=<r> (typed=<t> handlers=<h> foreign=<f> unread=<u> elsewhere=<e> deferred_bound=<d>)`. 5. Tests: update grpc.rs's `server_pass_matches_each_binding_shape_exactly_once` (Register-only cases: their line is a site, not an anchor) and `server_pass_registration_lines_join_one_marker_per_file` (`vec![4, 11]` / `vec![3, 8]` become anchors [4] / [3] plus sites [11] / [8]); add grpc.rs unit tests for each ImplArg form (Go `&T{}` / local / `pkg.NewServer()`, Python local over two branches, Node `.bind(this)` map and shorthand, an inline arrow handler). engine/tests/grpc_register_impl.rs (new; picked up by build.rs into engine_tests, FH.18) builds the fixture's tree and asserts its expect / forbid rows and the `register_impl` EVIDENCE on a Go impl STRUCT that embeds no Unimplemented base and lives in another file of the package. 6. Fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/grpc-register-impl-handlers/ (new); grade on HEAD before the fix (AUTHORING.md steps 3-4).

packets.title: Go implicit IMPLEMENTS stays inside one Go module: graph:iface pairs a type and an interface of different nearest go.mod roots only when every compared signature names no package-local type (predeclared or import-qualified only); the go.mod roots reach build_go through the Go build group
packets.rationale: FD.3c's edge audit (dev-notes/edge-precision-0.5.4.md, IMPLEMENTS|derived p 0.800, 6 of 30 wrong, all microservices-demo): `graph:iface` rules `method_signature` (2, type level) and `same_name` (4, method level) pair a genproto client of one service with the same-named interface of another service's genproto copy (src/shippingservice cartServiceClient -> src/productcatalogservice CartServiceClient; frontend productCatalogServiceClient::GetProduct -> checkoutservice's). Each service is its own Go module, so `*GetCartRequest` in the two copies are distinct types that share text. The method-level same_name edges ride on the type-level pair (`emit_method_level_implements_with` walks IMPLEMENTS edges), so gating `emit_go_implicit_implements` removes both. The pass knows package directories (GoPackages) but not module roots: `build_go(repo, parses)` takes none, and the CA.3b reachability gate (R2) applies only to one-method sets and test sides, so a multi-method interface whose signature text matches pairs across modules. The probe reproduces it at HEAD c4152966 and keeps a legitimate cross-module control (an imported interface with predeclared-only signatures).

packets.implementation: 1. Module roots into the Go build: `GroupCtx` gains `go_module_dirs: &'a [String]` (the repo-relative root dirs of the repo's GoModules, `""` for the repo root, sorted), filled at every GroupCtx construction (engine/src/build/assemble.rs, engine/src/build/mod.rs, engine/src/watch.rs, and lang_build.rs's test) from the repo's `GoModules` (`go_modules_for`, already computed beside each); `hidden_fp` in engine/src/watch.rs hashes it into the go group's fingerprint (it is a builder input; the exhaustive destructure fails to compile until it joins). `build_solo`'s go arm calls a new `glia_graph::build_go_with(repo, parses, go_module_dirs)`; `build_go(repo, parses)` stays as `build_go_with(repo, parses, &[])` (additive API; graph tests keep calling it; graph/src/lib.rs's `pub use build::*` exports the new fn, so no facade edit). 2. The gate (graph/src/build.rs `emit_go_implicit_implements`, after R1 and before R2): module_of(dir) = the longest module root (its `/` turned into `::`) that is `dir` or a `::`-segment prefix of it, else None. When both the type's and the interface's package dirs have a module and they differ, keep the pair only when it is `checked` (every signature compared, CA.3a) and no compared signature, on either side, holds a package-local named type: an identifier token of the signature text that is not a Go predeclared type (bool, byte, rune, string, error, any, comparable, int/int8..64, uint/uint8..64/uintptr, float32/64, complex64/128) and is not the selector half of a qualified `pkg.T` name. Otherwise skip it and count `cross_module`. No module dirs known (`&[]`), or either side outside every root -> unchanged. Read the exact `nav.method_sigs` text format first (CA.3a normalisation) and write the tokenizer to it. 3. Marker: `filtered_marker` gains `cross_module=<c>`: `[iface] go implicit filtered: signature=S scope=P (one_method=O test_side=X) cross_module=C signature_checked=K`. 4. Tests: a graph/src/build.rs unit test over two module dirs (same-module pair kept, cross-module package-local pair dropped, cross-module predeclared-only pair kept, `build_go` with no dirs unchanged); engine/tests/go_module_iface.rs (new; collected into engine_tests by build.rs, FH.18) builds the fixture's tree and asserts every expect / forbid row, the method-level `same_name` twins included. 5.
